title: SDK telemetry sampling and observability contracts - PRD
body:
Summary:
This PRD defines a pragmatic, privacy-conscious telemetry sampling and observability contract for the Hosted API SDKs (Node, Python, and mobile JS). The goal is to provide operators and product teams with high-fidelity signals for streaming responses, incremental structured output, and tool-calling behavior while keeping telemetry volume and PII risk bounded.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Current telemetry is noisy: we either capture everything (high cost) or sample too aggressively (miss regressions in streaming/tool flows).
- Incremental outputs and tool calls produce many micro-events per request; naive ingestion increases cost and makes dashboards hard to interpret.
- Customers and compliance teams require minimal exposure of user content; telemetry should avoid storing identifiable text without explicit allow-lists.
- SDK ergonomics are inconsistent across platforms (no consistent sampling override API, different batching semantics), making instrumenting apps difficult.

Goals:
- Define a cross-SDK event taxonomy and minimal schema for streaming, tool calls, and structured-output lifecycle events.
- Provide an adaptive sampling strategy that preserves edge-case detection (errors, regressions) while keeping per-customer event budgets predictable.
- Offer clear SDK primitives for: enabling/disabling telemetry, attaching correlation IDs, overriding sampling, and consent-aware redaction hooks.
- Ensure observability surfaces in Console: sampled traces, aggregation of tool-call latencies, partial-response error rates, and structured-output schema drift indicators.

Non-goals:
- Full tracing platform or replacing OpenTelemetry — we will interoperate with OTLP where feasible but focus on telemetry shape and sampling decisions.
- Long-term retention policies (this will be passed to infra/observability later).

Event taxonomy (flat, short names):
- request.start: high-level request received by runtime (metadata only)
- request.end: final status, token counts, model variant, cost estimate
- stream.chunk: partial output chunk emitted (metadata only, no full raw text by default)
- tool.call.start: SDK tool invocation start (tool name, input hash, correlation id)
- tool.call.end: tool result summary (status, latency, error code)
- structured.validate: schema validation result for structured outputs (schema id, pass/fail, diffs)
- cache.hit / cache.miss: KV/prefix cache events (key hashes, latency)
- sampling.signal: internal signal emitted when sampling decision was taken (reason)
- sdk.error: SDK-side errors (serialization, handshake failures)

Minimal event schema (fields allowed, value types described inline):
- event_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id (hashed), correlation_id, event_type, model_family, route, duration_ms, tokens_input, tokens_output, status, error_code, sample_rate, meta_tags
- content_field: NOT captured by default. If captured it must be redacted/hashed and flagged with consent_level in meta_tags.

Sampling strategy (high-level):
1) Deterministic reservoir by tenant+route: stable sampling ratio per tenant to ensure consistent dashboards. Default baseline: 0.5% of all synth requests, 5% of streaming requests, 25% of tool calls. These baselines are tunable per tenant by Console.
2) Priority overrides (always sample): any event that meets one or more criteria is force-sampled:
   - sdk.error or tool.call.end with non-200 status
   - structured.validate fail
   - request latency > 99th percentile for the model/route
   - explicit developer opt-in via sampling_override API
3) Adaptive uptick: when error spikes detected in a tenant, sampling multiplier automatically increases (x10) for 1 hour for that tenant and route to collect diagnostic signals.
4) Reservoir burst-cap: to avoid runaway ingestion, tenant-level daily event cap applied; Console shows estimated consumption and warns when limits approached.

Sampling determinism and reproducibility:
- SDK should use a deterministic sampling key computed from tenant_id + stable request hash to decide inclusion when in deterministic mode. This preserves longitudinal comparability in dashboards.

Privacy and data minimization:
- Default behavior: no user content (raw prompts, responses) is included in telemetry. Only token counts and hashed identifiers are allowed.
- Redaction hooks: SDKs expose a redact_hook(client_content) -> {allow_capture: bool, redacted_text: string, content_hash}. SDK implementer must mark captured content with consent_level: explicit | consented | none.
- PII allow-list: Console-managed allow-list where verified customers can opt into content-level telemetry for a bounded period; requires legal approval.

SDK ergonomics and developer API proposals:
- Global config (hosted-sdk.init): { telemetry: { enabled: true, sample_rates: {default:0.005, streaming:0.05, tool_calls:0.25}, redact_hook: fn, tenant_token: string } }
- Per-call overrides: call({..., telemetry: {force_sample:true|false, sample_reason:"string"}})
- Correlation helpers: sdk.new_correlation_id() and attach_correlation_to_context(ctx, id) to propagate IDs across retries and tool calls.
- Batching and flush semantics: SDK buffers telemetry events and flushes by (a) size (32 events) or (b) time (2s); SDKs must implement exponential backoff and disk-backed short-term queue for mobile/edge.
- Lightweight telemetry shim for low-footprint clients: minimal event envelope + UDP-like fire-and-forget; guaranteed best-effort only.

Streaming-specific considerations:
- stream.chunk events are sampled at a separate streaming rate; when a stream is sampled we capture stream.chunk meta for the entire session (sequence numbers, per-chunk durations, schema-validation markers) to allow reconstructing partial response timelines.
- If a stream triggers a priority override (e.g. structured.validate fail), SDK escalates and captures an annotated trace including the chunk indices and tool-call correlation points.

Tool-calling specifics:
- Tool calls are a major source of diagnostic info; capture tool.call.start/end with: tool_name, tool_interface_version, input_hash, latency_ms, status, error_code, tenant_route.
- Sensitive tool inputs must be hashed and only kept in telemetry when consented. Tool adapters in the SDK should implement a standardized adapter contract exposing metadata to telemetry without exposing raw content.

Structured output and schema drift detection:
- Integrate structured.validate events into the sampling pipeline: when sampled, include schema_id, validation_errors_summary, and a compact "schema-diff-hash" to detect drift trends without shipping full payloads.
- Console will compute per-schema failure-rate, top failing routes, and histogram of field-level missingness over sampled events.

Console / Observability surfaces required in phase 1:
- Tenant overview: sampled requests/day, estimated telemetry consumption vs cap, error spikes heatmap
- Streaming timeline view: sampled stream traces with chunk timing and tool-call overlay
- Tool-call dashboard: top tools by calls, p50/p95 latency, error-rate by tool and tenant
- Schema drift alerting: when structured.validate fail rate increases >X% absolute or >Y fold in 24h
- Sampling audit view: for a tenant show sampling configuration history and recent sampling.signal events

Operational constraints & cost control:
- Default tenant cap: 500k telemetry events/day; overspend requires billing/SA intervention.
- Tiered retention: sampled event traces retained 7 days by default, aggregated metrics retained 90 days.
- Ingress enforcement: telemetry gateway enforces per-tenant caps and applies default downsampling if upstream misbehaves.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0–2: SDK public API prototypes (Node + Python) and internal experiments capturing sample decisions only (no content).
- Week 3–6: Integrate reservoir-based deterministic sampling, priority overrides, and redact_hook implementation. Internal dogfood on platform-prod with Canary tenants.
- Week 7–10: Console dashboards for sampled traces, tool-call metrics, and sampling audit. Expose per-tenant sampling controls.
- Week 11–14: Mobile JS lightweight shim and opt-in PII allow-list flow (legal signoff).

Metrics for success:
- Signal-to-noise: proportion of sampled events that lead to actionable insights (target > 15% first-month for canary tenants).
- Cost predictability: sampled event volume within +/- 20% of Console estimate after 2 weeks for canary tenants.
- Incident triage time reduced: average time to identify root cause for streaming regressions reduced by 30% in tenants with sampling enabled.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Reservoir sizes vs deterministic sampling window: what window length preserves reproducibility without locking in old behavior?
- How aggressive should adaptive uptick be for noisy tenants to avoid telemetry storms?
- Concrete PII redaction heuristics — rely on heuristic detectors, or require developer-supplied redact_hook?

Next steps / owner tasks:
- Product (Jordan): finalize event taxonomy and publish lightweight JSON schema for events (no PII fields allowed by default).
- Eng SDK (Ravi): implement sdk.init telemetry config and per-call override prototype (Node + Python).
- Backend/observability (Elena): implement sampling.gateway with per-tenant caps and sampling.signal sink.
- Legal & Security (Maya): draft PII allow-list process and audit checklist.

References and inspiration:
- Prior internal doc: hosted-api-incremental-response-telemetry-spec-and-developer-checklist (see linked artifacts)
- OpenTelemetry best practices for sampling and cost control
- Internal Console team retention and cap policy notes

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative: prefer too little captured content over too much. We can widen capture later via opt-ins.
- Expect SDK ergonomics iterations after initial dogfood; keep APIs minimal and stable.
